summary: Migrate SpendCube from a Streamlit+SQLite prototype to a production-grade React+FastAPI+Supabase web application. All six phases of the Python analytics pipeline (ingestion, supplier harmonisation, categorisation, cube building, recommendations, review workstation) are preserved in their entirety — a FastAPI backend wraps the existing src/ modules as a thin HTTP adapter. The frontend is rebuilt in React+TypeScript with shadcn/ui and Recharts for a professional client-facing dashboard. Multi-tenancy is achieved via an engagement_id column on all database tables scoped per client. The result is a stable, deployable application that can be handed to a client with a URL, login credentials, and their CSV data.

decisions.monorepo_structure: frontend/ and backend/ directories are added alongside the existing src/ directory. All pipeline logic in src/ is preserved untouched and imported by the FastAPI backend via sys.path. Tests in tests/ continue to run against the original code.
decisions.parquet_eliminated: Parquet files are not used in v2. All cube data is served live from Postgres views/aggregations. This removes filesystem state from the deployment and makes the architecture cloud-native.
decisions.database_adapter: src/models/database.py get_engine() is extended to accept a full SQLAlchemy URL (not just a SQLite file path). When SUPABASE_DATABASE_URL env var is set, the backend uses Postgres; when absent it falls back to SQLite. This is backwards-compatible — all existing tests continue to pass.
decisions.multi_tenancy: engagement_id UUID column is added to all five existing tables (transactions, supplier_master, supplier_match_log, category_overrides, audit_log) plus a new engagements table. All queries in the backend are scoped to the authenticated engagement_id. Supabase RLS enforces this at the DB layer.
decisions.background_jobs: FastAPI BackgroundTasks handles pipeline execution asynchronously. A new pipeline_jobs table stores job status (queued/running/done/failed). The frontend polls GET /ingest/status for progress. This avoids Celery/Redis complexity for the initial deployment.
decisions.charts_library: shadcn/ui for UI primitives (cards, buttons, tables, forms, badges, dialogs) and Recharts for all charts (BarChart, AreaChart, PieChart, ComposedChart). Both are TypeScript-native and Tailwind-compatible.
decisions.frontend_state: TanStack Query v5 (React Query) for all server state. Provides caching, background refetch, and optimistic updates without a custom state management layer.
decisions.auth_strategy: Supabase Auth (email+password). JWT is included in all API requests via Authorization header. The FastAPI middleware validates the JWT using the Supabase JWT secret and extracts the user email. engagement_id is stored in the engagements table scoped to the user email.
decisions.deployment_targets: Vercel for the React frontend (zero-config, SPA routing via vercel.json). Railway for the FastAPI backend (Dockerfile-based deploy). Supabase cloud for Postgres + Auth. All secrets via environment variables — no hardcoded values anywhere.
decisions.savings_rates_yaml: The savings_rates.yaml and keyword_rules.yaml reference files remain in data/reference/ and are read by the Python pipeline at runtime. The backend mounts the data/ directory as a read-only volume in production.

existing_tables.transactions: 45-column table storing all canonical transactions post-ingestion. All Text types for IDs and dates (Postgres-compatible). Needs engagement_id column added.
existing_tables.supplier_master: Canonical supplier records keyed on canonical_supplier_id (SHA256 hash). Needs engagement_id column added.
existing_tables.supplier_match_log: Audit trail of supplier matching decisions with review_status field. Needs engagement_id column added.
existing_tables.category_overrides: Human-reviewed category correction rules keyed on canonical_supplier_id or gl_account. Needs engagement_id column added.
existing_tables.audit_log: Change history for all DB mutations. Needs engagement_id column added.
existing_tables.engagements: NEW table: id UUID PK, name TEXT, client_name TEXT, currency_label TEXT, engagement_title TEXT, owner_email TEXT, is_admin BOOLEAN, llm_dry_run BOOLEAN, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ.
existing_tables.pipeline_jobs: NEW table: id UUID PK, engagement_id UUID FK, status TEXT (queued/running/done/failed), stage TEXT, started_at TIMESTAMPTZ, completed_at TIMESTAMPTZ, error_message TEXT.

patterns_to_follow: All existing pipeline classes accept an engine: Engine parameter — follow this pattern in the backend adapter rather than creating global state
Confidence bands (HIGH>=0.85, MEDIUM>=0.60, LOW<0.60) are defined in src/models/schema.py ConfidenceBand — reuse these thresholds in API response payloads

userStories.title: Supabase SQL schema migration — all tables with engagement_id and Postgres views
userStories.description: Write the SQL migration that creates the full SpendCube v2 schema in Supabase (Postgres). This is the authoritative database definition for the v2 application. The schema adds engagement_id to all five existing tables, creates two new tables (engagements, pipeline_jobs), and defines five Postgres views that replace the Parquet cube files from v1. Row Level Security policies are added to enforce engagement isolation.
acceptanceCriteria: Create file: supabase/migrations/001_initial_schema.sql

Migration creates table engagements: id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), name TEXT NOT NULL, client_name TEXT NOT NULL, currency_label TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'AUD', engagement_title TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Procurement Spend Diagnostic', owner_email TEXT NOT NULL, is_admin BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false, llm_dry_run BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true, recommendations_json TEXT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()

Migration creates table pipeline_jobs: id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), engagement_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES engagements(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'queued', stage TEXT, started_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(), completed_at TIMESTAMPTZ, error_message TEXT

Migration creates table transactions with all 45 columns from src/models/database.py (transaction_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, source_system TEXT, source_row_number INTEGER, ingested_at TEXT, last_modified_at TEXT, invoice_number TEXT, document_type TEXT, invoice_date TEXT, raw_supplier_name TEXT, raw_supplier_id TEXT, raw_line_description TEXT, original_amount DOUBLE PRECISION, original_currency TEXT, base_amount DOUBLE PRECISION, base_currency TEXT, fx_rate DOUBLE PRECISION, gl_account TEXT, cost_centre TEXT, raw_payment_terms TEXT, payment_terms_days INTEGER, po_number TEXT, business_unit TEXT, plant_site TEXT, canonical_supplier_id TEXT, canonical_supplier_name TEXT, canonical_supplier_confidence DOUBLE PRECISION, parent_company_id TEXT, parent_company_name TEXT, category_l1 TEXT, category_l2 TEXT, category_l3 TEXT, unspsc_code TEXT, category_confidence DOUBLE PRECISION, category_method TEXT, spend_type TEXT, addressability TEXT, managed_status TEXT, is_credit_note INTEGER, is_intercompany INTEGER, is_tax_line INTEGER, is_duplicate INTEGER, review_status TEXT, reviewer TEXT, review_notes TEXT, review_date TEXT, raw_data TEXT) PLUS engagement_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES engagements(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

Migration creates table supplier_master: canonical_supplier_id TEXT NOT NULL, engagement_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES engagements(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, canonical_name TEXT, parent_company_id TEXT, parent_name TEXT, country TEXT, identifiers TEXT, created_at TEXT, updated_at TEXT, PRIMARY KEY (canonical_supplier_id, engagement_id)

Migration creates table supplier_match_log: id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, engagement_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES engagements(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, raw_supplier_name TEXT, raw_supplier_id TEXT, canonical_supplier_id TEXT, match_method TEXT, confidence DOUBLE PRECISION, evidence TEXT, review_status TEXT, created_at TEXT

Migration creates table category_overrides: id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, engagement_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES engagements(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, canonical_supplier_id TEXT, gl_account TEXT, override_l1 TEXT, override_l2 TEXT, override_l3 TEXT, unspsc_code TEXT, reviewer TEXT, reason TEXT, created_at TEXT

Migration creates table audit_log: id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, engagement_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES engagements(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, table_name TEXT, record_id TEXT, field_name TEXT, old_value TEXT, new_value TEXT, changed_by TEXT, changed_at TEXT

Migration creates indexes: CREATE INDEX ON transactions(engagement_id); CREATE INDEX ON transactions(engagement_id, invoice_date); CREATE INDEX ON transactions(engagement_id, canonical_supplier_id); CREATE INDEX ON transactions(engagement_id, category_l1); CREATE INDEX ON supplier_match_log(engagement_id, review_status); CREATE INDEX ON pipeline_jobs(engagement_id, status)

Migration creates view v_by_supplier: SELECT engagement_id, canonical_supplier_id, canonical_supplier_name, parent_company_name, COUNT(*) AS transaction_count, SUM(base_amount) AS total_spend, AVG(payment_terms_days) AS avg_payment_days FROM transactions WHERE COALESCE(is_intercompany,0)=0 AND COALESCE(is_tax_line,0)=0 GROUP BY engagement_id, canonical_supplier_id, canonical_supplier_name, parent_company_name

Migration creates view v_by_category: SELECT engagement_id, category_l1, category_l2, category_l3, unspsc_code, COUNT(*) AS transaction_count, SUM(base_amount) AS total_spend, COUNT(DISTINCT canonical_supplier_id) AS supplier_count FROM transactions WHERE COALESCE(is_intercompany,0)=0 AND COALESCE(is_tax_line,0)=0 GROUP BY engagement_id, category_l1, category_l2, category_l3, unspsc_code

Migration creates view v_by_month: SELECT engagement_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', invoice_date::date) AS month, SUM(base_amount) AS total_spend, COUNT(*) AS transaction_count FROM transactions WHERE COALESCE(is_intercompany,0)=0 AND COALESCE(is_tax_line,0)=0 GROUP BY engagement_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', invoice_date::date)

Migration creates view v_by_bu: SELECT engagement_id, business_unit, cost_centre, SUM(base_amount) AS total_spend, COUNT(*) AS transaction_count FROM transactions WHERE COALESCE(is_intercompany,0)=0 GROUP BY engagement_id, business_unit, cost_centre

Migration creates view v_by_payment_terms: SELECT engagement_id, CASE WHEN payment_terms_days <= 30 THEN '0-30' WHEN payment_terms_days <= 60 THEN '31-60' WHEN payment_terms_days <= 90 THEN '61-90' ELSE '90+' END AS bucket, COUNT(*) AS transaction_count, SUM(base_amount) AS total_spend FROM transactions WHERE payment_terms_days IS NOT NULL AND COALESCE(is_intercompany,0)=0 GROUP BY engagement_id, bucket
Migration enables RLS: ALTER TABLE engagements ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; (repeat for all 7 tables)

Migration creates RLS SELECT policy on transactions: CREATE POLICY select_own_engagement ON transactions FOR SELECT USING (engagement_id IN (SELECT id FROM engagements WHERE owner_email = auth.jwt()->>'email')). Repeat equivalent policies for INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on all 7 tables.
Create file: supabase/README.md — documents: npx supabase login; npx supabase link --project-ref <ref>; npx supabase db push to apply migration

userStories.title: FastAPI auth middleware + engagements CRUD endpoints

userStories.title: Ingestion API endpoints — file upload, column mapping, and async pipeline execution
userStories.description: Implement the three ingestion endpoints that power the upload wizard. The first endpoint parses headers from a CSV/Excel file without running the pipeline. The second endpoint kicks off the full pipeline as a FastAPI background task with engagement_id scoping. The third returns job status. The _run_pipeline function chains the existing src/ pipeline modules (Ingestor, harmoniser, SpendCategoriser, SpendCubePipeline) using the Postgres engine and engagement_id.
acceptanceCriteria: Create file: backend/app/routers/ingestion.py — APIRouter with prefix='/api/engagements/{engagement_id}/ingest', tags=['ingestion']
Add sys.path manipulation at top of ingestion.py: import sys, os; sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..', '..', '..')) to make src/ importable

POST /upload — UploadFile via Form; validates extension is .csv or .xlsx (else 400); saves to /tmp/spendcube_{uuid}.{ext}; reads first 2 rows to detect headers (pandas read_csv nrows=1 or read_excel nrows=1); returns {job_id: str(uuid4()), file_path: str, columns: list[str], row_count_estimate: int}

POST /run — body: {job_id: str, file_path: str, column_mapping: dict[str,str]}; validates engagement ownership; INSERTs row into pipeline_jobs with status='queued', engagement_id=engagement_id; calls background_tasks.add_task(_run_pipeline, engagement_id, job_id, file_path, column_mapping); returns {job_id, status: 'queued'}
GET /status/{job_id} — SELECTs pipeline_jobs row WHERE id=job_id AND engagement_id=engagement_id; returns {job_id, status, stage, started_at, completed_at, error_message}; 404 if not found

Create function _run_pipeline(engagement_id: str, job_id: str, file_path: str, column_mapping: dict, config_path: str = 'config.yaml'): (1) UPDATE pipeline_jobs SET status='running', stage='ingesting' WHERE id=job_id; (2) load config via load_config(config_path); (3) get engine via get_engine(os.environ['SUPABASE_DATABASE_URL']); (4) call init_db(engine) to ensure tables exist; (5) run Ingestor with engagement_id injection; (6) UPDATE stage='harmonising'; (7) run harmoniser; (8) UPDATE stage='categorising'; (9) run SpendCategoriser; (10) UPDATE stage='building_cube'; (11) run SpendCubePipeline (output_dir=None to skip Parquet); (12) UPDATE status='done', completed_at=now(); wrap in try/except: on exception UPDATE status='failed', error_message=str(e)
Add startup event in backend/app/main.py: on startup, UPDATE pipeline_jobs SET status='failed', error_message='Server restarted' WHERE status='running' — prevents stuck jobs after restart
Register ingestion router in backend/app/main.py

Create file: backend/tests/test_ingestion_api.py — tests: (1) POST /upload with valid CSV returns columns list, (2) POST /run creates pipeline_jobs row with status=queued, (3) GET /status/{known_id} returns job row, (4) GET /status/{unknown_id} returns 404
Verify: pytest backend/tests/test_ingestion_api.py -v — all tests pass

risks: Pipeline Postgres compatibility (US-004/US-005): The existing src/ modules were written and tested against SQLite. Postgres has stricter type handling for date casting (invoice_date is stored as TEXT — the v_by_month view casts it as ::date which will fail if any rows have non-ISO date strings). Mitigation: run the full integration test (python src/utils/generate_test_data.py --rows 1000 && full pipeline) against a local Postgres instance before declaring US-005 done.

sentence-transformers model size (US-005 Dockerfile): The all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model is ~90MB and is downloaded during docker build. This makes the backend image large (~1.2GB). Mitigation: pre-download in Dockerfile RUN step as specified in US-015, so the model is cached in the image layer and not re-downloaded at container startup.

RLS policy correctness (US-002): Supabase RLS policies using auth.jwt()->>'email' require the anon/service key to match the JWT issuer. A misconfigured policy will silently return empty results (not 403). Mitigation: test RLS using Supabase Studio SQL editor with a test JWT before going live.

FastAPI BackgroundTasks reliability (US-005): In-process tasks do not survive a worker restart. If Railway restarts the backend mid-pipeline, the job will be stuck in 'running'. Mitigation: the startup event in US-005 resets stuck jobs to 'failed' on boot. Acceptable for v1.

SpendCubePipeline Parquet output (US-005): src/cube/pipeline.py likely writes Parquet to output_dir. In v2 we want DB-only output. Review pipeline.py to check if output_dir=None is a valid no-op or if it raises an error. If Parquet output is mandatory, pass output_dir='/tmp/spendcube_parquet_{job_id}' and discard the files.
CORS in production (US-001): Initial CORS allows all origins. Before any client-facing deployment, set ALLOWED_ORIGINS to the Vercel deployment URL only.
outOfScope: Real-time collaboration — multiple analysts editing the same engagement simultaneously
Email notifications — notifying analysts when a pipeline job completes
Celery/Redis job queue — FastAPI BackgroundTasks is sufficient for expected volumes
Multi-file ingestion — merging multiple CSV files into one engagement
PDF report export — Excel export of recommendations is sufficient for v1
White-label theming — custom logos and colour schemes per client
SSO / enterprise auth — SAML, Google SSO, LDAP. Email+password is sufficient for v1
Mobile-responsive layout — targets desktop/laptop screens (1280px+) only
Streamlit dashboard preservation — dashboard/ is superseded by this sprint and does not need to be maintained
Real-time dashboard updates — data refreshes on page load or manual refresh button; no WebSocket streaming
